newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slides on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slides on crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday on Wednesday following a big drop in overnight crude values with the market still concerned about the prompt physical overhang, traders said.
"The market is down this morning mainly because of crude," one broker said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.80/$24.90 per barrel while July was at $24.75/$24.85, down 20 cents for the front month from Monday's quotes, brokers said.
July was down 10 cents from Monday leading to a narrowing of the June/July time spread to five cents from a traded 10 cents on Tuesday.
July gas oil traded earlier in the day at $24.75, brokers said.

Traders said backwardation narrowed on concerns that the market will not be able to absorb all the prompt physical cargoes, coupled with concerns over the opening of the arbitrage leading to four cargoes being fixed from the Mediterranean.

The physical market is in contango with cargoes loading 15 days forward offered at 40 cents below those loading 30 days out which traded on Tuesday at $25.30 per barrel for June 29-July 3 lifting, they said.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted down about 50 cents per tonne at $100.00/$101.50 because of the big crude drop.

Overnight July Brent crude closed down 62 cents to $18.90 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange. The after-hours ACCESS trading system traded down 21 cents from the official close on NYMEX to be last traded at $20.12 per barrel.
